Subject: Initial redlines for reseller onboarding addendum

Danielle —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As discussed, attaching our first-pass redlines to the reseller/marketplace addendum so your legal team can review. High-level notes up front:

- We aligned the revenue split and commission schedule in the order form; redlines focus on the pass-through billing language and liability carve-outs.
- We proposed a single-source-of-truth clause for metering to avoid dual-meter disputes (section 3.2).
- We tightened the indemnity language so it relates to Redwood’s hosted API misuse only (not unrelated third-party software).

Next steps I’m proposing:
1) Nimbus legal reviews our doc and returns comments by EOD Tue (6/22).
2) If there are non-negotiables, flag them and we’ll loop in our ops/legal and Karthik to triage.
3) Ben — can you prepare a 1-page procurement summary (billing routing, tax responsibilities, expected invoice cadence) to attach for their finance team?

Attachments: nimbus_msaa_redlines_v1.docx (redline), OrderForm_Example.xlsx (sample numbers)

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we want to get you onto Dedicated capacity by July.

Best,

Laura Bennett
Account Executive — Strategic Partners
Redwood Inference

From: Danielle Carter <danielle@nimblsys.com>

Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial redlines for reseller onboarding addendum

Laura —

Thanks for the redlines and the walkthrough. Quick questions from our side after a first pass:

- The metering single-source clause looks sensible; do you have a fallback if Redwood and Nimbus disagree on usage numbers for a billing period?
- Your indemnity carve-down is okay, but our finance team prefers language that preserves marketplace liability carve for resold software. Can we see a version that keeps a limited reseller liability in place?
- Can you confirm whether the reseller will be issued invoices from Redwood or from the marketplace (we need the billing flow to match our ERP).

I’m attaching Nimbus’ partner paper (v2) — it shows our standard PO/PO-acceptance timing and how we handle pass-through fees. Procurement will want to match that to the Order Form.

If we can get answers by Tuesday we’ll be in good shape for Legal to return consolidated comments.

Thanks,
Danielle

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Initial redlines for reseller onboarding addendum

Laura / team —

Thanks for looping us in. Quick internal summary and recommended positions to present to Nimbus:

1) Metering disputes: propose a "metering reconciliation" process with a 30-day cure window that permits either party to raise a dispute and use the platform logs as the authoritative source. If unresolved, tie to an independent auditor or a pre-agreed math formula. This avoids open-ended escrow/driving to litigation.

2) Limited reseller liability: we can accept a capped reseller liability but must carve out liability for Redwood’s gross negligence and for customer data breaches arising from Redwood-hosted infrastructure. Proposed cap: greater of $250k or 6 months of average monthly fees.

3) Billing flow: prefer Redwood-sent invoices to the reseller (Nexus/tax reasons), but can support marketplace-passthrough where Nimbus invoices end customers and remits to Redwood. Need their procurement to confirm ERP constraints.

Action items for Laura:
- Share the high-level reconciliation wording and liability cap as recommended language (I’ll draft legal-friendly text if they signal they’re open).
- Push Daniel(lle) for procurement contact and PO templates.

I’ll stand by to draft redline language once they confirm which model they prefer.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Carter <danielle@nimblsys.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 13:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial redlines for reseller onboarding addendum

Danielle —

Appreciate the quick reply and the partner paper. Answers inline below, plus a short one-pager attached for your procurement team to speed review.

> On Fri, Jun 18, 2027 at 10:03 AM Danielle Carter <danielle@nimblsys.com> wrote:
>
> The metering single-source clause looks sensible; do you have a fallback if Redwood and Nimbus disagree on usage numbers for a billing period?

Yes — we recommend a two-step approach: 1) automatic reconciliation against Redwood platform logs within 14 days after invoice; 2) if either party disputes, a 30-day dispute window where we both exchange supporting logs and attempt to reconcile. If still unresolved, the parties agree to an independent technical auditor (mutually selected) to certify the usage. We can include an optional cap on disputed adjustments (e.g., adjustments limited to 6% of the invoice unless fraud is suspected).

> The indemnity carve-down is okay, but our finance team prefers language that preserves marketplace liability carve for resold software.

Understood. Our legal is willing to accept a reseller cap for general commercial liability. Karthik suggests the cap be the greater of $250k or six months of average monthly fees, but Redwood will not relinquish carve-outs for gross negligence, willful misconduct, or Redwood-hosted data breaches. We’ll draft alternative phrasing showing both: (A) Redwood-preferred (narrower), and (B) a compromise with the capped reseller liability. Please advise which you prefer so we can circulate the actual redline.

> Can you confirm whether the reseller will be issued invoices from Redwood or from the marketplace (we need the billing flow to match our ERP).

We can support both flows in practice, but for a smooth initial implementation we recommend Redwood invoicing Nimbus directly and Nimbus handling downstream billing. This keeps tax/treatment consistent and reduces reconciliation friction the first quarter. If Nimbus needs the marketplace invoicing model, we’ll mark the Order Form and include the technical mapping in the onboarding packet.

Next steps:
- I’ve attached a one-pager (OrderForm_Billing_onepager.pdf) that Ben prepared covering invoice cadence, tax responsibility, and an example remittance flow for ERP teams.
- Danielle — please send your procurement contact and PO template (if different from the partner paper) and confirm whether the liability cap is acceptable or whether you need alternate language.

Thanks — aiming for Legal pass-back by Tue so we can land a signature in July.

Best,
Laura

Attachments: OrderForm_Billing_onepager.pdf (procurement summary)
From: Danielle Carter <danielle@nimblsys.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@nimbus-sys.com

Laura / Karthik —

Appreciate the clear options. Procurement is OK with the reconciliation process and the auditor fallback — that will work with our ERP team. On liability, procurement and legal are asking for the negotiated cap to be the greater of $500k or six months of fees (they prefer a higher floor given our customer exposure). Is Redwood able to consider $500k floor?

I’m attaching our PO template (Nimbus_PO_template.xlsx) and looping procurement (procurement@nimbus-sys.com) for headcount and tax onboarding.

We’ll aim to return a consolidated redline by Tue EOD with any final asks.

Thanks — Danielle
